questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless all of these are true:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle is fast enough to pass.

questions.explanation: You need all three things to pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street: clear visibility ahead, time to return to your lane safely, and a car that can pass quickly. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The car whose driver sounds the horn first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control devices, you must yield to vehicles coming from your right.

questions.question: You come to a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic pass, then go when safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is correct?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They may use loudspeakers to give directions.
They may follow each other closely.

questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances using sirens and flashing lights. Follow any directions they broadcast. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: When changing lanes, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police about road conditions ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police about road conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and use your turn signal. Look for other drivers in your path. Never use your phone while driving.

questions.question: A green arrow with a red light means:

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow allows you to drive only in that direction if the intersection is clear of traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make about 200 decisions per mile. Any extra activity takes your focus away from driving and creates danger.

questions.question: A driver turning left must yield to a bicycle coming from the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to bicycles just as you would to cars coming toward you. Keep your wheels straight while waiting and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?
questions.explanation: Slow down on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning. Keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, take your foot off the gas. Do not brake. Keep the vehicle straight and let it slow down on its own.

questions.question: What are HOV lanes reserved for?

options.text: Vehicles with more than one person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles with more than one person.
questions.explanation: HOV stands for High Occupancy Vehicles. HOV lanes are for vehicles with more than one person inside. Signs show how many people must be in the vehicle and when the rule applies.

questions.question: What are signs that tell drivers about dangerous conditions called?
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to dangerous conditions ahead. Follow warning signs for your safety. Ignoring a warning sign can cause an accident.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough room to safely pull back in front.

questions.question: What must you do when a school bus ahead is stopped to pick up or drop off children?

options.text: Stop completely until all children have left the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops with flashing red lights and a stop arm extended, you must stop completely. Do not move until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in. Even after the bus moves, wait to make sure no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not allowed?

options.text: On or near a curve or hill.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet ahead in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near a curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians, which could cause a crash.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up as fast as you can.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, let any pedestrians and traffic still in the intersection cross safely.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in school zones?
questions.explanation: The speed limit in school zones is 15 miles per hour. Drive carefully in areas where children may be present.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When are collisions most likely to happen?

options.text: When all vehicles travel at about the same speed.
When one lane of traffic moves faster than other lanes.
When one vehicle travels faster or slower than the other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one vehicle travels faster or slower than the other traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster than traffic increases crash risk. Driving slower than traffic also causes crashes because other drivers may rear-end you or swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal medicines (prescription or over-the-counter). Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.
questions.explanation: You must use a turn signal every time you pull away from a curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends or road narrows ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends or road narrows ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is narrowing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other roadside objects.
